newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL AND WIMBLEDON BID TO CLOSE GAP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LIVERPOOL AND WIMBLEDON BID TO CLOSE GAP.

text.p: Liverpool and Wimbledon aim to take advantage of this weekend's World Cup fixtures to close in on Arsenal at the top of the English premier league on Saturday.
Arsenal's scheduled match against Southampton was played earlier this month to allow the London side's internationals to play for their countries this weekend.
Arsenal won 3-1 and are now four points clear of Liverpool and Wimbledon, who both play their one match in hand on the leaders on Saturday.

Liverpool host troubled Middlesbrough in a dress rehearsal for next month's League Cup quarter-final, while Wimbledon, unbeaten in their last 18 games, entertain 1995 champions Blackburn, starting to stir after a disastrous start to the season.

Liverpool, beaten 1-0 at home by Sheffield Wednesday last weekend -- their first league defeat at Anfield in over a year -- welcome back striker Stan Collymore and England midfielder Jamie Redknapp from injury.

Brazilian Emerson is likely to play for Middlesbrough following his recent return to Teesside -- the latest chapter in a tug-of-war between his commitment to his family and his commitment to his club.
Emerson had gone to Brazil to be with his sick wife and refused to return to England until she was better.

'Boro need Emerson's undeniable talent after a depressing run of three goalless performances which has seen them slip dangerously close to the relegation zone. His compatriot Juninho is still nursing a knee injury and may well miss out.
Wimbledon are suddenly being considered championship material after their astonishing run of success, and even down-to-earth manager Joe Kinnear is starting to become excited.

"My dreams and ambitions are no different to those of somebody like Alex Ferguson (Manchester United manager)," he said. "If we are in a position to win the title with six games to go then I would back us strongly to do it."
"But it is a worry now that other people seem to be beginning to take it for granted that we will now definitely be in that position. I know that it is still going to take a hell of a lot more work."

Wimbledon will be without captain Vinnie Jones, who joins the Welsh squad for their World Cup qualifier against Turkey. Brian McAllister is likely to replace Jones in midfield with Robbie Earle taking the captain's arm-band.
Chelsea's Mark Hughes is also with the Welsh squad, despite having eight stitches in a gash in his shin just a fortnight ago, and he might still play for both club and country at the weekend.
Wales play in Cardiff on Saturday while seventh-placed Chelsea face Sunderland on Sunday.
"We will keep in touch with (Wales) over the weekend before deciding whether to fly Mark up to Sunderland," Chelsea assistant manager Gwyn Williams said.
"We don't know if Mark will play for Wales and, if he does, whether he would be fit to play another match the following day."
